subject: Token handling and invoice atomization for short-call pilots
summary: External asks on rounding, minimums, and how KV cache reuse affects invoicing; proposed concession and sample calculations attached; follow-up meeting requested.
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@nimbly.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token handling and invoice atomization for short-call pilots

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for walking through the pilot profile this week. A couple of the procurement questions you raised (rounding, minimums, and how long context is accounted for across short calls) came up with Finance — I put a short summary attached and a CSV with worked examples (redwood_billing_summary.pdf, token_examples.csv).

High-level:
- We meter per-token generated + input with per-request rounding to the nearest 10-token quantum by default, but for short-call pilots we can propose an adjusted floor to avoid noisy microcharges.
- KV cache reuse is eligible for a prefix credit that reduces billable input tokens when requests reuse recent conversation context (see examples).
- Context-length (how we decide whether context is stitched into the same billable session) is driven by 1) contiguous session id and 2) time gap threshold (default 30 minutes).

Proposal (pilot concession):
- 10-token rounding replaced with a 50-token minimum per request for the pilot period; any request under 50 tokens will be billed as 50.
- KV-prefix reuse credit: when a request reuses a cached prefix from the same session within 30 minutes, we subtract cached input tokens up to the length of the prefix (not to exceed 50% of the request) before applying the 50-token floor.
- Streaming responses: we bill tokens as emitted; the 50-token floor still applies per request, except for streaming heartbeat-only pings which are free under the pilot.

If that aligns broadly with your expectations we can lock this in for the first 60 days and then reconcile on actual token distributions. I can also walk through the CSV examples on a short call — does Monday at 10am PT work?

Attachments: redwood_billing_summary.pdf (proposal + examples), token_examples.csv (row-level math)

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales - Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks for the quick write-up and the CSV. A few clarifying questions before we accept the pilot concession:

1) That 50-token floor — is it per API call or per logical user session? Our usage is many tiny inference calls (~15–40 tokens) per user action. If per-call, that could still be hefty at scale.
2) Can you confirm how the KV-prefix credit is detected? We have multi-user threads where prefixes may overlap across users; we need guarantees that credits only apply within the same user/session id.
3) How do you handle the first request that seeds a prefix? Will that initial seeding be charged fully and then subsequent requests get credits?
4) For auditability, can we get a sample invoice line that shows how a batch of 1,000 small calls would appear after credits/floors?

If you can answer these in writing and share a one-page sample invoice we can expedite procurement. Monday 10am PT works for a quick walkthrough.

—Nikhil
VP Product, NimblyAI

Subject: Re: Token handling and invoice atomization for short-call pilots

Nikhil — great questions. Answering inline and attaching a one-page sample invoice in the PDF: see the sample invoice section of redwood_billing_summary.pdf. Short answers below, then a couple of worked examples.

1) 50-token floor scope: per API call. Rationale: it simplifies invoicing and caps line-item noise for pilots with many tiny requests. Concession path: if after 60 days we see >80% of requests below 50 tokens and the effective cost is prohibitive, we'll consider switching to an amortized per-session floor (open to a volume-triggered change).

2) KV-prefix credit detection: credits are only applied when the request contains a session-id that matches the cached prefix owner. We do not cross-credit across different session-ids. That matches your requirement for per-user guarantees.

3) Seeding the prefix: the initial request that creates a prefix is billed normally. Subsequent requests that reuse the prefix within the 30-minute window receive the credit as described (we apply cached-input-subtraction before flooring).

4) Sample invoice: attached (redwood_billing_summary.pdf). Example from token_examples.csv (excerpt):
- Scenario A: 1,000 calls × 30 tokens input + 10 tokens model output = 40 tokens each. Without concession = 40 tokens × 1,000 = 40,000 tokens billed. With 50-token floor per call = 50 × 1,000 = 50,000 tokens billed.
- Scenario B (50% prefix reuse): of the 1,000 calls, 500 reuse a 20-token prefix. For those 500 calls we subtract 20 tokens before applying floor: (40 - 20 = 20) => floor to 50 so billed = 50 for each of the 500. Total billed = 50*1,000 = 50,000 (same as pure floor in this example because subtraction still left under floor). Where prefix reuse is large relative to the request size you can see the delta in the CSV.

A few process notes: finance will reconcile pilot usage weekly and we can produce a line-level CSV for auditing. If you want a separate pilot SKU (flat monthly pool + overage) we can propose that as an alternative — Camila and Vanessa can scope numbers with your procurement team.

I'm good for Monday 10am PT. I'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Markus
